source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. The First Steps — Stone Age
points: **Prehistory** = the very long period before writing. Known only from material remains (tools, bones, cave art).
**Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age):** hunter-gatherers; rough stone tools; nomadic.
**Mesolithic (Middle Stone Age):** smaller tools (microliths); **Bhimbetka** (Madhya Pradesh) rock shelters have famous **rock paintings**.
**Neolithic (New Stone Age):** polished tools; beginning of **agriculture** and **domestication of animals** → **first villages** and settled life.

sections.heading: 2. Mehrgarh — An Early Village
points: **Mehrgarh** (in the Baluchistan region) is one of the **earliest farming villages** in the subcontinent.
Evidence of early wheat/barley cultivation, domesticated animals, mud-brick houses and burials.
Marks the transition from hunting-gathering to **settled farming** — the base on which cities later grew.

sections.heading: 3. The Harappan (Indus–Sarasvati) Civilisation
points: India's **first cities** — also called the **Indus Valley** or **Indus–Sarasvati** Civilisation; a **Bronze Age** civilisation.
**Mature phase:** c. 2600–1900 BCE.
Named after **Harappa**, the first site to be excavated.

sections.heading: 4. Features of Harappan Cities
points: **Town planning:** streets in a **grid** pattern, meeting at right angles; a raised **citadel** and a **lower town**.
**Drainage:** covered drains along streets — a very advanced system.
**Standardised baked bricks** in a fixed ratio, used everywhere.
**Great Bath** at Mohenjo-daro; **granaries/warehouses**; **water reservoirs** at Dholavira.
**Seals** (often of steatite, with animal motifs and an **undeciphered script**); standardised **weights**; beads, pottery and toys.
**Trade** — with distant lands including **Mesopotamia** (which called the region **Meluhha**).

sections.heading: 5. Life, Crafts and Decline
points: **Crafts:** bead-making, pottery, metal-work (copper, bronze), shell and cotton — **cotton** was among the earliest here.
**Lothal** (Gujarat) had a **dockyard** — a centre of maritime trade.
**Decline** (after c. 1900 BCE): possibly climate change, drying of the **Sarasvati** river, floods or shifting trade — no single cause; cities were gradually abandoned.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Stone Age order: Palaeolithic → Mesolithic → Neolithic; agriculture began in the **Neolithic**.
Bhimbetka = rock paintings (Mesolithic); Mehrgarh = earliest farming village.
Harappan = first cities, Bronze Age; mature phase c. 2600–1900 BCE.
Largest site = Rakhigarhi (Haryana); Great Bath = Mohenjo-daro; dockyard = Lothal; reservoirs = Dholavira.
Harappan script = undeciphered; seals = steatite; Mesopotamian name for the region = Meluhha.
Brick ratio standardised (length:breadth:height = 4:2:1).

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: Agriculture began in the **Neolithic**, NOT the Palaeolithic.
The **largest** Harappan site is **Rakhigarhi**; the **dockyard** is at **Lothal** — don't swap sites.
The Harappan **script is undeciphered** (we cannot read it).
It was a **Bronze Age** civilisation (copper + tin), not Iron Age.
